title: Dynamic Bucket Prioritization for capacity-constrained roadmap
creator: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary:

This ticket proposes and tracks an experiment to introduce a Dynamic Bucket Prioritization (DBP) framework for Redwood's product roadmap. DBP augments RICE-style scoring with capacity-aware buckets and continuous latency/cost penalty signals so that we prioritize work not only by expected impact but also by the production economics and short-term capacity constraints. The goal is an automated, transparent per-cycle prioritization surface that product managers and Eng leads can iterate on during planning and post-mortem cycles.

Why this is needed:
- Current RICE-like decks rank by reach/impact but lack an explicit mechanism to throttle high-latency or high-cost initiatives when Dedicated/hosted capacity is constrained.
- Teams are making ad-hoc tradeoffs between feature value and token economics, which leads to overcommitting GPU-bound initiatives early in the quarter.
- We need an operationalizable rubric that blends expected customer value with per-unit inference economics so that shipping decisions align with OKRs and capacity constraints.

What DBP does (high level):
1) Bucketization: classifies candidate initiatives into three dynamic buckets for the upcoming cycle: Expand (scale-up, low-cost-per-user), Optimize (improve performance/cost of existing features), Protect (reliability/compliance and high-SLA items). Buckets are rebalanced each cycle based on OKR signals and capacity forecasts.
2) Score augmentation: compute a base RICE score (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) and then apply two multiplicative modifiers: a latency penalty and a cost elasticity factor. These modifiers are derived from the model-serving forecast for the cycle (e.g., token-volume projections, peak-seconds-by-region).
3) Capacity-aware cutoff: each bucket has a soft capacity allocation for the cycle (e.g., 55% Expand, 30% Optimize, 15% Protect) which can be nudged by PM/Eng. Projects are accepted into a bucket until the projected token-hours budget is reached.

Formal scoring formula (prototype):
DBP_score = RICE_base * (1 - L_penalty) * (1 - C_penalty) * Bucket_priority_multiplier
- RICE_base = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort
- L_penalty = sigmoid((projected_95p_latency_increase - latency_threshold) / latency_scale) * latency_weight
- C_penalty = clamp((projected_token_cost_delta / cycle_budget), 0, 1) * cost_weight
- Bucket_priority_multiplier is a small tuning scalar (1.1, 1.0, 0.9) depending on strategic bucket weights set by the PM.

Operational details and data inputs:
- Inputs required from teams: reach estimate, quantified impact (customer-facing metric), confidence justification, effort points, projected inference token volume, projected latency amplification (p95), and estimated token-cost delta.
- Data sources: runtime forecast dashboard (token volumes), Console cost breakdown (per-model unit cost), recent latency histograms, and Dedicated capacity forecasts.
- Default weights: latency_weight=0.6, cost_weight=0.4 (configurable per-cycle by PM).

Evaluation plan (experimental rollout):
- Phase 1 (2 cycles): run DBP in shadow mode for two planning cycles; compare accepted projects vs. old prioritization and gather stakeholder feedback.
- Phase 2 (1 cycle): enforce capacity-aware cutoffs on non-critical buckets; require explicit PM/Eng exceptions for override.
- Phase 3: integrate DBP into the canonical planning spreadsheet and the roadmap dashboard (console).

Success metrics:
- Fewer late-cycle scope deferrals due to capacity overcommit (target: reduce by 60% by end of Q2).
- Improved alignment between top-priority work and OKR key results (qualitative PM survey > 4/5).
- Reduction in projected token-cost overshoot from planned to actual (target: <10% variance).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: teams may game projections to avoid penalties. Mitigation: require historical calibration and penalize repeated >25% variance between forecast and actual.
- Risk: over-weighting latency/cost could starve feature velocity. Mitigation: cap penalties and allow manual bucket overrides with justification and leadership approval.

Next steps and deliverables tracked in this ticket:
- Draft DBP scoring spreadsheet template and example calculations (deliverable: sheet link).
- Implement a shadow DBP ranking script that pulls forecast inputs and outputs a ranked list (deliverable: prototype script + README).
- Run stakeholder review cycle with Eng leads, Design, and Growth to validate reach/impact definitions.
- Wireframe roadmap dashboard changes to show bucket allocations and token-budget consumption.

Links and artifacts:
- Planning sheet (prototype): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/dbp-prioritization-prototype
- Prototype script repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prioritization-dbp (PRs: #402, #410)
- Forecast dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/forecast-token-hours

Open questions:
- What is the right cadence to rebalance bucket allocations mid-cycle? (weekly, biweekly, or only at cycle boundaries)
- Should we include hard ceilings for single-project token-budget as % of total cycle budget? If so, what % (recommended 15-25%)?
- How do we model long-lived infra investments that amortize cost over multiple cycles?

Owners and communication plan:
- PM owner: Aisha Kapoor (handles weighting, stakeholder sync)
- Eng owner: Liam O'Connor (implements prototype script and charts)
- Stakeholders: Eng leads, Design, Growth, Solutions Engineering
- Stakeholder review date: 2026-03-20

Notes on transparency: every project's DBP inputs and resulting score will be stored as a row in the planning sheet and a CSV export available to the execs and Eng leads to enable audits and calibration.
